blocks.text: Plugins publish sandboxed — they run isolated and can’t touch site data directly. A reviewer verifies and signs yours before it can run trusted.

v{data.listing.latestApprovedVersion} is what installs today. It keeps installing until a reviewer approves this one — nobody is upgraded onto unreviewed code, and nothing you publish here can change a version already installed.

fields.label: Bundle (.js)
fields.help: One self-contained bundle. It’s parsed and checked before publishing — forbidden APIs, size, and every network call against the origins your manifest declares.

fields.label: Description
fields.help: The one-line summary on browse cards

options.label: None

fields.label: README
fields.help: Shown on your listing page — what it does, how to configure it, and what it reads, stores or sends. Reviewers and cautious buyers read this first.

fields.label: Changelog
fields.placeholder: Fixed the timer drift on Safari; added a compact layout
fields.help: Two audiences: the reviewer, comparing this version against the last approved one, and every installer who reads it on your listing’s changelog tab before updating. On a first version there is nothing to compare against — say what the plugin does instead, or leave it.

fields.label: Repository URL
fields.help: The source for this bundle. A reviewer opens it first — it is what the repository confirmation below is about.

fields.label: License
fields.help: Short label, e.g. MIT or Apache-2.0

fields.label: Who can install this

options.label: Anyone — publish to the marketplace
Only this organization — private plugin

fields.help: Private is a choice about audience, not about trust — it takes the identical review path.

fields.label: Price (USD)
fields.help: 0 for free, or $3 and up for a paid listing. Paid listings need payouts set up.

fields.label: Before you publish

options.label: The repository URL is public and contains the source for this bundle
options.detail: A reviewer opens it first. A repo that 404s, is private, or holds something unrelated is the cheapest reason a submission gets sent back.

options.label: A license is included and I have the right to publish this code
options.detail: Missing or incompatible licensing is a legal problem for every workspace that installs it, not only for us.

options.label: The README documents what data this plugin reads, stores or sends, and where it goes
options.detail: Anything the plugin does with member or page data belongs in the README before it is installed, not in a support thread afterwards.

options.label: Every declared network host is required — I have removed the ones I do not use
options.detail: Declared hosts become this plugin’s CSP connect-src. An allowlist wider than the plugin needs is the single most common thing review sends back, and it widens the blast radius if the bundle is ever compromised.

options.label: I have tested this version on a site I control
options.detail: These exact bytes, not an earlier build. Static review cannot tell a reviewer what your plugin does at runtime.

options.label: Neither my listing nor any text on my elements disparages Aglyn, quotes what its plans cost, or sells a way around one
options.detail: Saying which Aglyn plans or features your plugin needs, or works with, is fine and useful. Editorialising about Aglyn’s prices or quotas, stating or implying what a plan contains, or pitching this version as a way to avoid a plan or an upgrade is not. This covers any text you supply that renders in — or ranks within — the console, not only the listing: an element’s name, description, tags, search keywords and attribute labels all ship inside your bundle, and a customer meets them in their own element picker. Search terms count even though nobody reads them, because they decide which element gets shown.

fields.label: Before you publish

options.label: The repository URL is public and contains the source for this bundle
options.detail: A reviewer opens it first. A repo that 404s, is private, or holds something unrelated is the cheapest reason a submission gets sent back.

options.label: A license is included and I have the right to publish this code
options.detail: Missing or incompatible licensing is a legal problem for every workspace that installs it, not only for us.

options.label: The README documents what data this plugin reads, stores or sends, and where it goes
options.detail: Anything the plugin does with member or page data belongs in the README before it is installed, not in a support thread afterwards.

options.label: Every declared network host is required — I have removed the ones I do not use
options.detail: Declared hosts become this plugin’s CSP connect-src. An allowlist wider than the plugin needs is the single most common thing review sends back, and it widens the blast radius if the bundle is ever compromised.

options.label: I have tested this version on a site I control
options.detail: These exact bytes, not an earlier build. Static review cannot tell a reviewer what your plugin does at runtime.

options.label: Neither my listing nor any text on my elements disparages Aglyn, quotes what its plans cost, or sells a way around one
options.detail: Saying which Aglyn plans or features your plugin needs, or works with, is fine and useful. Editorialising about Aglyn’s prices or quotas, stating or implying what a plan contains, or pitching this version as a way to avoid a plan or an upgrade is not. This covers any text you supply that renders in — or ranks within — the console, not only the listing: an element’s name, description, tags, search keywords and attribute labels all ship inside your bundle, and a customer meets them in their own element picker. Search terms count even though nobody reads them, because they decide which element gets shown.

options.label: The changelog describes what changed since the last version
options.detail: An update is where something slips through — the first version gets read closely, the fourth rarely does. Saying what moved is what makes reviewing a diff possible.
